authorization: Researcher asked the program to step back from narrow phase-diagram optimization, use the reference literature, and identify scientifically important next questions.
question: After the selector-rate route closes at three exact obstructions, which literature-supported theorem interface, if any, can directly control the physical posterior-sector balance at the square midpoint?
claim_boundary: This is a theorem-interface and research-direction audit. It may select a falsifiable next lemma, but it cannot establish midpoint noncorrectability or a threshold without a matched proof or experiment.
alternatives: Random-cluster, RSW or disjoint-occurrence results applied to a correctly identified physical posterior observable.
Planar alpha-orientation, flow-lattice, cycle-reversal or log-concavity results applied to the restricted logical switching graph.
Finite-width transfer, large-deviation or spectral results used only for a controlled strip statement, not a two-dimensional threshold.
planned_steps: Search the local reference archive and Wiki first, then targeted primary sources for each theorem family.
Write a hypothesis-by-hypothesis applicability matrix against full charge, majority weighting, logical-sector action and size-uniformity.
Select at most one next lemma only if all hypotheses are matched; otherwise close the route and name the scientifically larger alternative question.
acceptance_criteria: Every candidate theorem is tied to a primary source and its actual hypotheses, not only a method name.
The matrix explicitly checks the two-configuration selector law, physical majority conditioning, logical-sector flip and thermodynamic uniformity.
A next lemma is promoted only if its hypotheses survive existing exact counterexamples; otherwise the selector route is closed as non-priority.
No literature analogy or fixed-width statement is promoted to a square midpoint or threshold theorem.
stop_rule: Stop after twelve primary sources and three existing exact counterexamples, or earlier when one hypothesis-complete theorem interface is found. Do not collect new LER data or reopen the bounded selector computations.
decision: Nine primary sources across random-cluster/disjoint occurrence, planar orientation/flow and finite-width transfer were checked against the physical posterior law. None matches all required hypotheses. The selector route is demoted; the next central question is the decoder-independent logical-sector free-energy-gap distribution.
